item.title: 5 European Hotels Where You Can Beat the Heat
item.description: Whether hidden in the mountains or nestled by the sea, these spots offer some respite from the continent’s high temperatures.
item.dc:creator: Adam H. Graham

item.title: How a Deadly Storm Surprised Wisconsin Boaters
item.description: Three children died last weekend when a storm whipped up 80 mile-per-hour winds and large waves on Geneva Lake in Wisconsin.
item.dc:creator: Amy Graff

item.title: U.S. Department of Energy Underestimated Potential Los Alamos Plutonium Leak Danger, Study Finds
item.description: An accident at the lab that produces America’s nuclear bomb cores could lead to more fatalities than previously estimated by the federal government, according to new research.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Inez Guzmán
item.media:credit: Nina Riggio for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico is home to the country’s only active plutonium-handling facility.

item.title: At Least 12 People Die in Southern Spain Wildfire
item.description: The blaze in Andalusia, one of the deadliest on record in the country, also left more than 20 people missing. Many of the victims were foreign tourists, the Spanish authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Barragán
item.media:credit: Infoca, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: A still from a video provided by the Andalusia Wildfire Service of the wildfire in Los Gallardos district, Spain, on Friday.

item.title: Western Europe Had Its Hottest June on Record
item.description: An unusually early heat wave smashed records across France, Britain and Spain. Temperatures in some areas are starting to soar again.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Zhong
item.media:description: Riding a hot train in London on June 24. Average temperatures across Western Europe last month were 3.05 degrees Celsius, or 5.5 degrees Fahrenheit, above the mean from recent decades.

item.title: Hotter Seas in Britain and Europe Threaten Marine Life
item.description: Higher sea temperatures have followed scorching weather across Europe, prompting Britain’s weather service to declare a “severe” marine heat wave.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Wolfe
item.media:description: People diving into the English Channel in Brighton, on the south coast of England, during a heat wave last month.

item.title: Here’s How Much Rain Fell Across the New York Area This Week
item.description: After a blistering heat wave, a dousing of heavy rain this week caused flooding across the region. Experts said it could have been worse.
item.dc:creator: Judson Jones
item.media:credit: Angelina Katsanis for The New York Times
item.media:description: Storm damage in Brooklyn on Monday.

item.title: Inside the United States’ Billion-Dollar Blind Spot: Hail
item.description: Scientists have never quite understood how hail works. Meet the storm chasers trying to change that.
item.dc:creator: Judson Jones

item.title: At Least 17 Dead in China After Flooding and Tornadoes During Typhoon Maysak
item.description: Videos showed inundated roads, farmland and buildings, and floodwaters rushing toward homes, while the region braced for a potential super typhoon this week.
item.dc:creator: Lily Kuo and Pei-Lin Wu
item.media:description: A flooded riverside near a wharf on the Yongjiang river in Nanning, in China’s southern Guangxi Province, on Monday.

item.title: Death Toll From Oppressive Heat in New Jersey May Be as High as 29
item.description: In New York City, emergency rooms last week logged the highest number of patients treated for heat-related illnesses in years.
item.dc:creator: Tracey Tully and Joseph Goldstein
item.media:description: Soccer fans sought a cool spot last week at a World Cup match at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

item.title: Heat Waves Are Taking a Big Toll on Chickens
item.description: The birds are particularly vulnerable to high temperatures, and France’s torrid June took a heavy toll.
item.dc:creator: Chico Harlan and Léontine Gallois
item.media:credit: Samuel Aranda for The New York Times

item.title: Extreme Heat Hits Europe for the Third Time This Year
item.description: It is continent’s third spell of scorching weather since May. Europe is the world’s fastest-warming continent.
item.dc:creator: Nazaneen Ghaffar and Natan Odenheimer

item.title: Wildfires Force Evacuation of Thousands in Southwest France
item.description: The blaze in the Pyrenees, a region bordering Spain, has scorched more than 11,000 acres so far.
item.dc:creator: Natan Odenheimer
item.media:description: A firefighting jet battling the flames in Ille-sur-Têt, France, on Monday.

item.title: Typhoon Bavi Pounds Guam and Northern Mariana Islands
item.description: There was an islandwide power outage on Saipan, the capital of the Northern Mariana Islands, as the Category 5 storm approached.
item.dc:creator: Nazaneen Ghaffar, Josie Moyer and Mar-Vic Cagurangan
item.media:description: Strong winds brought by Super Typhoon Bavi hit Guam on Monday.

item.title: NYC and New Jersey Brace for Heavy Rain and Flooding: Latest Forecast
item.description: On Monday, parts of New Jersey were underwater, downed trees were blocking roads in Connecticut and there was a flash flood warning in New York City.
item.dc:creator: Erin McCann, Nazaneen Ghaffar, Hilary Howard and Andy Newman

item.title: More Severe Weather Looms as Over 800,000 Remain Without Power
item.description: Strong storms knocked out power this week to customers from Oklahoma to Connecticut. As they waited on Sunday for the lights to come back on, the forecast called for more severe weather.
item.dc:creator: Johnny Diaz and Nazaneen Ghaffar
item.media:description: Lightning flashes in the sky during Fourth of July celebrations on Saturday in Washington. More than 800,000 customers across the United States remained without power on Sunday after a series of storms.

item.title: America Marks Its 250th Birthday With Storms, Sweat and Fire
item.description: Independence Day celebrations were canceled nationwide and the Brooklyn Bridge briefly caught fire. Yet Americans still found countless ways to celebrate.
item.dc:creator: Campbell Robertson
item.media:description: Fireworks erupt over the National Mall in Washington to cap off the day’s events — and extend into the next.

item.title: Guam and Northern Mariana Islands Prepare for Typhoon Bavi
item.description: Typhoon Bavi, a tropical cyclone barreling through the Pacific Ocean, was forecast to pass near the U.S. territories on Monday with the force of a Category 5 hurricane.

item.title: Crowds Evacuated as Storms Menace Washington Ahead of Trump Speech
item.description: Thousands of people stood in security lines for hours in severe heat to reach the National Mall, only to be ordered to leave as events were set to start. Some refused.
item.dc:creator: Campbell Robertson and Aishvarya Kavi
item.media:description: Thunderstorms headed toward Washington on Saturday evening, forcing evacuations of thousands at the National Mall.

item.title: The City Where You’ll Nearly Always Want a Jacket on the Fourth of July
item.description: As the East Coast bakes under a heat wave, San Francisco will be 66 degrees. But good luck watching the fireworks through the fog.
item.dc:creator: Amy Graff
item.media:credit: Christie Hemm Klok for The New York Times
item.media:description: A cloudy day in San Francisco last month.

item.title: Nathan’s Hot Dog Contest Captivates Coney Island Despite Heat Wave
item.description: Temperatures climbed above 90 degrees on Saturday, as Joey Chestnut and Miki Sudo once again reigned supreme.
item.dc:creator: Claire Fahy and Kaja Andric
item.media:description: Joey Chestnut was on pace to break his record early in the competition, but the heat appeared to slow him down. He still ate 66 hot dogs in 10 minutes.

item.title: It’s heat dome 1, George Washington 0.

item.dc:creator: Jennifer Schuessler
item.media:credit: Rachel Wisniewski for The New York Times
item.media:description: Independence Mall in Philadelphia, where a replica of George Washington’s field tent was slated to be pitched before plans where canceled because of the heat.

item.title: July Fourth Heat Wave Forecast: Latest Updates
item.description: The Midwest will get a break but temperatures for much of the East Coast will again climb above 100 degrees. Stay indoors as much as possible, experts said.
item.dc:creator: Amy Graff and Erin McCann
item.media:credit: Rachel Wisniewski for The New York Times
item.media:description: Edward Armstrong used a hand-held fan to cool himself after a parade in Philadelphia was canceled because of excessive heat on Friday.

item.title: To Beat the Heat, the Ultrarich Have Snow Rooms
item.description: Indoors, for a fortunate few, it’s always a winter wonderland.

item.title: The Texas Hill Country Flood, One Year Later
item.description: A year after a catastrophic flood killed 139 people in the Texas Hill Country, communities along the Guadalupe River are still rebuilding.
item.dc:creator: Edgar Sandoval
item.media:credit: Callaghan O'Hare for The New York Times
item.media:description: The banks of the Guadalupe River in Ingram, Texas, earlier this week. The river swelled during flash flooding last July that claimed 139 lives.

item.title: Fourth of July Weekend Presents a Huge Logistical Challenge for New York

item.media:credit: Lucia Vazquez for The New York Times
item.media:description: Tall ships traveled past the East River Esplanade in Manhattan during Sail4th 250 on Friday. Dozens of vessels are set to take part in a parade on the Hudson River on Saturday.

item.title: More Than 1 Million Without Power After Storms in Midwest and Northeast
item.description: Strong winds from thunderstorms began to cause widespread power losses on Friday. More than 1.3 million customers, from Oklahoma to Massachusetts, had no electricity late Saturday.

item.media:credit: Robert Killips/Lansing State Journal, via USA Today, via Imagn Images, via Reuters

item.title: 3 Children Dead After Boat Capsizes on Wisconsin Lake During Severe Storm

item.dc:creator: Mark Walker and Amy Graff
item.media:description: Lake Geneva, Wis., sits at the eastern end of Geneva Lake southwest of Milwaukee. The city is a popular weekend destination.
